audit_scope.method: For each final queue item, read its exact-v1 Review and claim boundary, then read the actual semantic-body binding in the current owner chapter plus the declared adjacent chapters. Check the old valid path, changed constraint, state/control owner, benefit, trade-off, failure mode, fallback/coexistence, evidence boundary, unique ownership, and placement before the first anchored level-two Review notes heading.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — the text starts from fixed action chunks, introduces variable physical execution horizons, separates model, controller and serving-scheduler authority, and states calibration, stale-action, fairness and sim-to-real risks. Short horizon plus deterministic control remains the safety fallback; the claim is limited to the disclosed robot configurations.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — PD disaggregation owns KV movement and role split; this chapter uniquely owns global scheduling of regenerate/execute rounds.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — entry request limiting remains the old valid path, while recursive agent fan-out changes the constraint. The runtime owns the component call graph and hard depth/cost/time bounds; learned energy is explicitly only a sensor. Tracing cost, threshold error and false positives are stated, with simple non-recursive services retaining request-local limiting.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — tenant isolation remains in chapter 71 and production release/readiness in chapter 73; amplification threat and enforcement evidence remain canonical here.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — immutable rebuild and atomic switch remain the simple baseline; continuous SSD updates introduce selective reads, entrance revision and cache identity. Index publication/crash recovery stays with the index owner, while retrieval only consumes published snapshots. Write amplification, invalidation and durability gaps are explicit, with immutable generations retained as fallback.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — chapter 75 owns per-call context assembly and chapter 77 persistent/derived memory; chapter 76 uniquely owns corpus/index search and maintenance state.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — full-sequence training is preserved as the semantic baseline, then deployment segmentation creates a training/runtime mismatch. Segment, mask, position, KV revision and gradient boundary become artifact identity; reduced backward state is exchanged for truncated long-range credit. Full backprop remains the fallback when remote gradients matter, and claims stay workload-bounded.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — decode cadence remains in chapter 44 and token-budget batching in chapter 46; chapter 45 uniquely owns cached state identity and lifecycle.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — request-local payment remains sufficient for synchronous low-value trusted settlement; asynchronous or external settlement requires binding action, payer/payee, amount, nonce, expiry, service outcome and receipt. The payment executor owns effect-time verification and reconciliation. Added latency, compensation and disputes are explicit, and the attack evidence is not generalized to every implementation.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — multi-tenancy and production rollout retain their owners; chapter 72 uniquely owns payment authorization, replay and settlement threat boundaries.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — global-norm clipping remains the cheap default guard; low-rank spectral outliers motivate clamping only leading singular values. Threshold, cadence, rank and approximation error become optimizer-side state. SVD cost, stale estimates and failed low-rank assumptions are stated, with global norm and root-cause diagnosis retained as fallback.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — data quality and supervised adaptation stay in chapters 27 and 29; chapter 28 uniquely owns pretraining optimization and gradient stabilization.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — end-to-end congestion control remains the normal path, while cross-DC collective tail makes its feedback loop too slow. Destination-side buffering owns flow/collective identity, order, expiry and failure semantics without claiming completion. Buffer exhaustion, reordering and a new failure domain are explicit; ordinary transport and conservative topology remain fallback.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — checkpoint recovery remains chapter 35 and tensor layout chapter 37; cross-DC collective execution remains canonical in chapter 36.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — FedAvg remains the direct baseline when architectures and parameter coordinates match. Heterogeneous private models change the exchanged state to versioned public-prompt behavior evidence and a coordinator-owned consensus artifact. Prompt coverage, pseudo-label error, privacy and malicious-client risks are explicit; parameter aggregation and independent privacy/Byzantine controls remain valid alternatives.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — checkpoint artifacts and tensor-parallel layout are not duplicated; chapter 36 uniquely owns distributed/federated coordination semantics.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — static payload scanning and one sandbox run remain the baseline; adaptive attacker feedback changes the object to a versioned mutation lineage with per-round side-effect receipts. The red-team runtime owns budget, environment and oracle state, while deterministic postconditions retain final authority. Cost and feedback-oracle leakage are explicit, with fixed low-privilege skills retaining the static path.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — tenant isolation and production release do not take over adaptive skill-admission threat modeling; chapter 72 remains the canonical security owner.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — random prompts and aggregate memorization remain a low-cost baseline but miss identity-targeted leakage. The release Gate binds principal coverage, attacker prefix, decoding and exposure surface, while data lineage connects remediation. Query cost, sensitive evaluation governance and false negatives are explicit; synthetic results are not treated as production exposure rates.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — chapter 71 owns tenant boundaries and chapter 73 release workflow; chapter 72 uniquely owns privacy threat/evidence semantics.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — a centralized provider remains simplest under a clear trust boundary; provider compromise changes identity, ACL, ordering and audit into Byzantine governance state. The control plane must declare fault threshold and select audit, monitoring, BFT or hybrid branches. Quorum latency, membership/key lifecycle and fail-closed behavior are explicit; consensus is not confused with output correctness.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — chapter 81 owns durable workflow state and chapter 83 protocol interoperability; chapter 82 uniquely owns multi-agent governance and delegation trust.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — native collectives remain the baseline; decoupled quantization/entropy coding introduces a device-side codec selector and overlapped execution plan. The runtime owns tensor identity, error/lossless contract, codec revision, order and fallback. Kernel overhead, incompressible distributions and convergence risk are explicit, with native NCCL retained for small payloads or fast links and benchmark claims kept workload-bound.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — checkpoint and tensor layout concerns stay in adjacent chapters; collective compression execution remains canonical in chapter 36.

items.mechanism_audit: Pass — hand-written EvalSpec, metric and deterministic verifier remain the auditable baseline for a small, stable task set. Rapid agent/framework/requirement divergence changes generated plan, metric code, trace parser, dependencies and report into a versioned evaluator artifact rather than an admitted scorer. The text preserves the complete draft → executable → non-vacuous → meta-evaluated → admitted chain: the generator owns only the proposal, the execution harness owns isolated reconstruction and Eval@1 receipts, the evaluation owner owns mutation/known-example checks and construct-validity admission, independent meta-evaluator/human anchors check disagreement, and the release owner alone commits promotion/hold/rollback. Reuse and trace coverage trade against instrumentation, storage, sandbox, latency and annotation cost; plan-code drift, API/schema mismatch, vacuous metrics and common-mode judge bias are explicit. Failed or drifting revisions fall back to manual EvalSpec/deterministic verifier or diagnostic-only status. Exact-v1 evidence is bounded to the disclosed six-stage EvalAgent, 20 agents × two requirement types, Claude-family backbones, pre-collected traces, 62.5–65.0% first-run executability and subjective meta-evaluation; it does not prove ground truth, cross-framework portability, admission-gate sufficiency or removal of human/verifier release authority, and the paper's repository lacks an event-time immutable commit.
items.adjacent_owner_audit: Pass — chapter 65 remains the resource admission/placement owner and explicitly hands useful-result evidence to chapter 66; chapter 67 owns observed runtime signals and explicitly denies itself the final quality decision. Generated-evaluator artifact admission therefore belongs uniquely to chapter 66, whose following paragraph keeps Evaluation Run evidence separate from release Decision authority.
